200	There is in us matter, which the angels do not have. We have
201	matter, we have a body,
202	and we are commanded to be
203	holy with our matter. In a certain sense this is
204	the higher
205	challenge, because that HaShem is holy
206	is simple, since not only is He not matter, but
207	He created both the matter and the spirit. That
208	the angels are holy is because there is no matter in them. We
209	are commanded to be holy even though we have matter,
210	and matter is not holy.
211	Rather, we are commanded, and this is the very deep thing
212	here, we are commanded to sanctify the matter,
213	and in this to be different from the nations of the world.
214	The human being,
215	all human beings in the world are built of body and soul,
216	of matter and spirit.
217	The verses that describe this are in the account of the creation of man,
218	in the book of Shemot, sorry, in the book of Bereshit, chapter 2, verse
219	7: "And HaShem Elokim formed man from the dust of the ground,
220	and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and man became a living soul."
221	So we need to know, we spoke about this in other lessons,
222	that all human beings in the world have a soul.
223	Every person, by the very fact of being a person, has a soul. There is
224	a distinction between the people of Israel and the nations of the world in the spiritual level
225	of the height of their soul, the
226	spiritual height.
227	But the nations of the world also have a soul.
228	The human being, but every person also includes a body, and a body is
229	matter. And matter,
230	in relation to spirit, is on a much, much
231	lower level.
232	Now of course the question is asked: how is it possible
233	that we, the people of Israel, the whole congregation of the children of Israel, who have
234	a body, who have matter, how can we be sanctified? What
235	does it mean, "You shall be holy"? What does it mean
236	to sanctify the matter?
237	So this is what we will try to learn today, and it is not so
238	simple, but we will try.
